stories.title: Shopoff Secures Approval for Buena Park Residential Development
stories.excerpt: Shopoff Realty Investments has secured unanimous approval from the Buena Park City Council for 5600 Beach Blvd, a 13.76-acre residential development in Buena Park. The property is currently occupied by the Amway Corporation with a corporate sale-leaseback in place until the end of 2026 and consists of two industrial buildings totaling approximately 370,031 square feet. “5600 Beach Blvd represents an important step forward for Orange County and is intended to help address the need for attainable and diverse housing options for first-time homebuyers and for Buena Park’s growing senior population,” said Shopoff Realty Investments’ president and CEO, Bill Shopoff. “Transforming an industrial site into a vibrant residential community aligns with the city and county’s evolving needs, providing homes for people at every stage of life.” The development aims to deliver 231 three-story townhomes and duplex units, offered with four different floor plans, along with 50 for-rent senior affordable housing units. Homes are expected to be delivered in 2029-2030. The post Shopoff Secures Approval for Buena Park Residential Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Shopoff Realty secures unanimous approval for 13.76-acre Buena Park mixed-use: 231 townhomes/duplexes, 50 senior affordable units.
Industrial-to-residential conversion addresses Orange County housing shortage; delivery 2029–2030.
Amway sale-leaseback expires end-2026; development clears land-use entitlement risk.
stories.summary: Shopoff Realty has won city council approval to convert a 13.76-acre industrial property in Buena Park, CA (currently leased to Amway through end-2026) into 231 for-sale townhomes and duplexes plus 50 senior affordable rental units. The project targets first-time homebuyers and seniors and aligns with Orange County's stated housing need. Deliveries are expected 2029–2030.
stories.impact: Signals strong municipal appetite for industrial-to-residential conversion in Orange County submarkets facing affordability pressure. A greenlit project with 2029 delivery windows suggests land cost and entitlement risk are lowering for similar adaptive-reuse plays in the region—relevant for mixed-income rental development timelines and competitive positioning in Orange County.

stories.title: Matawan Retail Trades to Private Investor for $15M
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of Park Plaza, a retail center in Matawan, NJ. The asset sold for $14.67 million. “Park Plaza attracted significant investor interest due to its diverse tenant mix, strong visibility and strategic location within one of Monmouth County’s most established retail corridors,” said Seth Goldberg, associate director investments in Marcus & Millichap’s New Jersey office. “Well-positioned neighborhood shopping centers with durable cash flow continue to be highly sought after, and this transaction reflects the sustained demand for quality retail assets in New Jersey.” Goldberg, Brent Hyldahl and Alan Cafiero of Marcus & Millichap marketed the property for the seller and procured the buyer, both private investors from New Jersey. Located at 343-351 State Rte. 34, the retail center sits on a 5.86-acre lot totaling 61,750 square feet. It was built in 1986 and contains 20 suites. The rent roll features a diverse mix of dining, lifestyle, retail and service-oriented tenants, including a Dunkin’ with a drive-thru. The post Matawan Retail Trades to Private Investor for $15M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Park Plaza retail center, Matawan NJ, sells for $14.67M (61,750 SF, 20 suites, built 1986).
Diverse tenant mix and durable cash flow attract private investor; neighborhood retail remains liquid.
No relevance to multifamily development.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap brokered the sale of Park Plaza, a 61,750-square-foot neighborhood retail center in Matawan, NJ, to a private investor for $14.67 million. The 1986-built asset contains 20 suites with mixed dining, lifestyle, and service tenants. The broker highlighted strong visibility, location in Monmouth County's retail corridor, and durable cash flow as drivers of investor interest.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Confirms retail market liquidity in NJ suburbs but no signal on residential demand, zoning, or financing conditions affecting apartment development.

stories.title: Dana-Farber Opens Outpatient Oncology and Hematology Clinic in Attleboro
stories.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Sturdy Health have opened a new clinic in Attleboro, offering expanded outpatient medical oncology and hematology care for patients in Southern Massachusetts. Dana-Farber will operate the new ambulatory cancer clinic within the newly constructed Sturdy Health Specialty Care Building on the Sturdy Health campus. The new center, with 10 exam rooms and 17 infusion beds, provides Dana-Farber’s level of care locally. In addition to medical oncology and hematology care and infusion, the clinic will offer genetic counseling, clinical trials, nutrition guidance, social work support, and other supportive services. “The opening of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute – Attleboro at Sturdy Health is an important milestone for patients and families across Southern Massachusetts,” said Jennifer Sutherby, VP & Healthcare Lead at Redgate, which managed the development. “Redgate is proud to have partnered with Dana-Farber and Sturdy Health to help plan and deliver a specialized healthcare destination that brings nationally recognized cancer care closer to the community.” The post Dana-Farber Opens Outpatient Oncology and Hematology Clinic in Attleboro appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute opens ambulatory clinic in Attleboro, MA; 10 exam rooms, 17 infusion beds.
New Sturdy Health Specialty Care Building expands healthcare access to Southern Massachusetts.
Healthcare facility development signals demand-driver but no direct impact on multifamily supply or rents.
stories.summary: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Sturdy Health opened a new outpatient oncology and hematology clinic in Attleboro, MA, housed in a newly constructed Sturdy Health Specialty Care Building. The clinic includes 10 exam rooms, 17 infusion beds, genetic counseling, clinical trials, and supportive services, bringing nationally recognized cancer care to Southern Massachusetts.
stories.impact: Signals healthcare facility investment in Attleboro but provides no direct signal on residential demand, job migration, or rental growth drivers relevant to multifamily development. Could modestly support population retention in area if clinic draws patients/families; watch for downstream healthcare-worker hiring and inbound migration.

stories.title: RAF Pacifica Group Acquires Fully Leased Retail in Downtown Encinitas
stories.excerpt: RAF Pacifica Group (RPG), a commercial real estate investment firm focused on acquiring and developing retail, industrial, mixed-use, and office properties across San Diego, has acquired a fully leased, five-tenant retail building at 548-568 South Coast Hwy. 101 in downtown Encinitas. The acquisition price was not disclosed. “Properties like this rarely make it to market, and when they do, they move fast,” says Adam Robinson, founder and president of RPG. “This one came to us because a tenant in the building heard the owner was considering a sale and reached out directly. They wanted us as their landlord.” The 4,939 square-foot building sits directly on Highway 101 in the 101 Shopping District, a walkable retail corridor a short distance from Moonlight State Beach. With a tenant base including three retail shops and two restaurants, the property had remained in the hands of the same family for more than six decades. The post RAF Pacifica Group Acquires Fully Leased Retail in Downtown Encinitas appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RAF Pacifica acquires fully leased 4,939-SF retail building in downtown Encinitas for undisclosed price.
Five-tenant property (3 retail, 2 restaurants) remained family-owned 60+ years; rare off-market transaction.
Retail deal; no direct multifamily impact.
stories.summary: RAF Pacifica Group acquired a fully leased, five-tenant retail building (4,939 SF) at 548–568 South Coast Highway 101 in downtown Encinitas, CA. The property, situated directly on Highway 101 near Moonlight State Beach in the walkable 101 Shopping District, had been family-owned for over six decades and came off-market via tenant referral.
stories.impact: No material relevance to multifamily development. Retail acquisition in Encinitas does not signal residential demand, zoning shifts, or capital allocation patterns affecting apartment projects in San Diego County.

stories.title: Foundation Alloy Moves to Woburn for First Dedicated Manufacturing HQ
stories.excerpt: Following its recent funding announcement, advanced metals company Foundation Alloy has selected 45 Industrial Pkwy. in Woburn, MA as the home of its first dedicated manufacturing headquarters..Relocating from MIT’s The Engine, the company has leased approximately 36,055 square feet, which will support the manufacturing, laboratory and research infrastructure needed to scale production and support its next phase of growth. The transaction was arranged by Cushman & Wakefield’s Kevin McNamara, Ross Gaudet and Michael O’Leary, who represented Foundation Alloy. JLL’s Chelsea Andre, Rachel Marks and Chris Decembrele represented the landlord, Camber Development and Wheelock Street Capital. “Foundation Alloy represents exactly the type of company driving the next generation of advanced manufacturing in Massachusetts,” said McNamara. “As companies transition from research and development into commercial-scale manufacturing, finding facilities with the right combination of power, infrastructure and flexibility becomes one of the biggest challenges to growth. 45 Industrial Parkway presented a rare opportunity to pair an exceptional building with an ownership group willing to invest alongside an innovative company.” The post Foundation Alloy Moves to Woburn for First Dedicated Manufacturing HQ appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Foundation Alloy (advanced metals) leases 36,055 SF manufacturing HQ in Woburn, MA; relocates from MIT.
Cushman & Wakefield and JLL arranged lease; landlords Camber Development and Wheelock Street Capital.
Tech/advanced manufacturing cluster expansion in Boston metro signals job inflow and rental demand growth.
stories.summary: Advanced metals manufacturer Foundation Alloy has leased approximately 36,055 square feet at 45 Industrial Parkway in Woburn, MA, establishing its first dedicated manufacturing headquarters after relocating from MIT's The Engine. The deal was arranged by Cushman & Wakefield for the tenant and JLL for landlords Camber Development and Wheelock Street Capital. The company plans to scale production and support R&D at the facility.
stories.impact: Advanced manufacturing expansion in greater Boston signals job creation and inbound talent migration to Woburn and surrounding Route 128 corridor submarkets. Expect upstream demand for workforce housing in inner-ring suburbs; multifamily developers should underwrite rental demand strength for 1–3-bedroom units targeting young engineers and manufacturing professionals in Woburn, Waltham, and adjacent communities.

stories.title: Longfellow Sells Hatch Life Sciences Building in LIC for $87M
stories.excerpt: Life sciences developer Longfellow Real Estate Partners has parted with its first-ever New York City project at a discount. Longfellow’s Hatch Life Sciences Building, located at 43-10 23 Street in Long Island City, Queens, has sold for $86.9 million, according to city records filed Friday. Pearl Realty Management’s Jack Guttman signed for the buyer, under the entity 4310 23 St. A representative of Pearl Realty Management did not respond to requests for comment. Longfellow purchased the existing building at 43-10 23 Street in 2021 alongside its partner, Steven Orbuch’s Sculptor Real Estate, for $92.5 million. Longfellow, led by CEO and co-founder Adam Sichol, planned to invest another $120 million into turning the former parachute manufacturing plant into a mix of life sciences labs and offices. Construction had all but wrapped up when Commercial Observer visited in 2024. The final product spanned over 208,000 square feet across seven floors, including prebuilt lab suites, modular research space and flexible office areas. Longfellow and Sculptor did not respond immediately to requests for comment on the sale. While Guttman’s plans for the purchase remain unclear, the landlord appears to be active in the Long Island City market. Recent purchases include the Standard Motors Product Building at 37-18 Northern Boulevard for $42 million and BrightSpire Capital‘s office building at 21-02 49th Avenue for $28 million. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Longfellow sells Hatch Life Sciences Building, LIC Queens, for $86.9M; purchased 2021 at $92.5M.
208,000-SF mixed lab/office conversion; Longfellow + Sculptor invested $120M additional cap ex.
Life sciences real estate value compression; distressed exit after 3-year hold suggests market softening.
stories.summary: Longfellow Real Estate Partners has sold the Hatch Life Sciences Building at 43–10 23rd Street in Long Island City, Queens, for $86.9 million—a $5.6 million loss from its $92.5 million 2021 acquisition. Longfellow and partner Steven Orbuch had planned to invest an additional $120 million to convert the former manufacturing plant into 208,000 square feet of lab suites, modular research space, and flexible office. The sale was completed by buyer 4310 23 St (Pearl Realty Management).
stories.impact: Life sciences lab market in Queens/LIC facing valuation pressure despite significant capital investment and completion. A pre-stabilization exit at a loss signals cap rate expansion, uncertain leasing velocity, or oversupply in LIC lab space. For multifamily developers: competitor lab conversions may stall, freeing up conversion-ready industrial buildings; but broader signal is capital flight from specialized flex/lab assets—monitor LIC multifamily absorption and rental rates for secondary market softening.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Buys Two Miami Affordable Housing Rentals
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from the Gatehouse Group, paying a combined $63.8 million, property records show. In the largest deal, the investor paid $34 million for the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments in the Naranja neighborhood, near the southern end of the county. Built in 2011, the 4.8-acre asset houses 20 three-story buildings at 25881 Southwest 143rd Court, just west of the South Dixie Highway. The sale breaks down to roughly $226,660 per unit. CBRE Capital Partners provided a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan. Across the county in Miami’s Little River neighborhood, Starwood paid $29.75 million for the 160-unit Lafayette Square complex. The 19-story building sits on a 1.2-acre site, a block west from Northeast Second Avenue at 150 Northeast 79th Street. The deal equates to about $185,900 per apartment. The Gatehouse Group appears to have retained ownership of the adjacent 136-unit property. The Mansfield, Mass.-based firm developed both the Lafayette Square and Magnolia Landing Apartments, completing the former in 2008 and the latter in 2011. Representatives for Starwood and Gatehouse Group did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management (Barry Sternlicht) acquires two Miami affordable rentals for $63.8M combined.
Magnolia Landing (150 units, Naranja, $34M; $226.7K/unit) and Lafayette Square (160 units, Little River, $29.75M; $185.9K/unit).
Institutional capital targeting Miami affordable housing; Freddie Mac financing supports underwriting.
stories.summary: Starwood Asset Management, led by Barry Sternlicht, acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from the Gatehouse Group for a combined $63.8 million. Magnolia Landing (150 units in Naranja, 2011-built) sold for $34 million ($226,660 per unit), and Lafayette Square (160 units, 19-story, Little River) sold for $29.75 million ($185,900 per unit). CBRE Capital Partners arranged a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan for Magnolia Landing.
stories.impact: Major institutional capital (Starwood, Freddie Mac) actively acquiring stabilized affordable multifamily in Miami-Dade at scale, signaling confidence in demographic demand and GSE-backed financing availability for workforce housing. Competitive signal: per-unit pricing ($186K–$227K) establishes market clearing rates for 2011+ vintage affordable assets; new development underwriting must compete against these cap rates. Watch for similar acquisitions as a yield-compression trigger for development feasibility in South Florida.

stories.title: Ad Agency Doubles Office HQ Space in Move to Hackman Campus in L.A.
stories.excerpt: An international advertising agency is more than doubling its office footprint with a new headquarters lease in El Segundo, Calif. Innocean USA signed the 101,000-square-foot deal at Hackman Capital Partners’ creative office campus in the small enclave just south of Los Angeles International Airport. The agency will relocate nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach after construction on its new space concludes in 2027, according to JLL, which represented the tenant. The company reportedly will use part of the space as a production facility for commercials and other content. Terms of the lease were not disclosed. “This move is about creating the right environment for our next chapter,” Innocean USA CEO Steve Jun said in a statement. “This is an investment in our people, our clients, and the future we’re building together.” The complex, named after its address at 888 Douglas Street, includes four buildings totaling 550,000 square feet over 30 acres. Hackman acquired the former Northrop Grumman aerospace manufacturing complex in 2016, and invested about $100 million converting it into the creative office. Other major occupiers at the property have included L’Oréal USA, which signed for more than 100,000 square feet in 2021, and Beyond Meat, which originally leased 280,000 square feet for its headquarters. Aerospace and defense companies have also returned to L.A.’s South Bay, and helped bolster leasing at the El Segundo campus. Hypersonic aircraft developer Hermeus signed for 62,552 square feet earlier this year, while Varda Space Industries expanded to 54,749 square feet in 2025. Innocean USA is the U.S. arm of Innocean Worldwide, which was created by Hyundai Motor Group. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham and Mitch Lundquist represented Innocean, while Hackman was represented in-house. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Innocean USA (advertising agency) leases 101,000 SF at Hackman Capital's El Segundo creative campus; 600-employee relocation.
Tenant relocating from Huntington Beach; build-out complete 2027.
Corporate HQ expansion signals talent/job inflow to LAX-adjacent submarket; modest residential demand driver.
stories.summary: International advertising agency Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot lease at Hackman Capital Partners' 888 Douglas Street creative office campus in El Segundo, CA, more than doubling its footprint. The company will relocate approximately 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach; construction concludes in 2027. The campus totals 550,000 square feet across four buildings on 30 acres.
stories.impact: Innocean's 600-employee net migration from Huntington Beach to El Segundo (LAX-adjacent) suggests modest workforce housing demand in greater El Segundo and Beach Cities submarkets. However, office tenant expansion (not relocation to new market) limits fresh demand signal. Monitor: if other ad/tech agencies follow to Hackman's campus, cumulative job base may support rental demand for young creative professionals and mid-level staff seeking housing near El Segundo.

stories.title: Attorney James Allen Joins Camber Property Group as Senior Counsel
stories.excerpt: Camber Property Group has onboarded a new general counsel for its affordable housing and community development transactions, Commercial Observer has learned. James Allen has decamped from real estate law firm Hirschen Singer & Epstein and started the new role this week assisting Camber with affordable housing projects in New York state and the New York tri-state region, according to the development firm. “One trend I am seeing is that, in their efforts to solve the ongoing housing affordability crisis, more developers are starting to expand both the types of projects that they participate in and their geographic footprint,” Allen said in a statement. “Camber is always thinking creatively about both, but they present unique challenges.” Allen was previously an associate for four years at Nixon Peabody and a senior staff attorney for the New York Court of Appeals. The Brooklyn Law School graduate also pens articles about housing equity and affordability while serving on the board of the New York Housing Conference’s Rising Leaders Network and the New York City Bar Association’s Housing & Urban Development Committee. Hirschen Singer & Epstein did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “I feel lucky to have the chance to expand upon that and work with many of the legal partners that I have learned from over the years, while Camber solidifies its New York presence and intentionally expands its footprint to other regions,” Allen said. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: James Allen joins Camber Property Group as senior counsel for affordable housing transactions.
Focus: NY state and tri-state region affordable development and community deals.
Personnel hire signals Camber expansion; no direct market or financing impact.
stories.summary: Attorney James Allen has joined Camber Property Group as general counsel for affordable housing and community development transactions across New York state and the tri-state region. Allen previously spent four years at Nixon Peabody and served as senior staff attorney at the New York Court of Appeals. He is a Brooklyn Law School graduate and serves on the Rising Leaders Network of the New York Housing Conference.
stories.impact: No material impact on multifamily development markets, supply, demand, capital, or costs. Indicates Camber is scaling affordable housing practice in NY/tri-state but provides no signal on market conditions, financing, or competitive positioning.

stories.title: Selldorf Architects Renews 14K-SF 860 Broadway Lease for 10 Years
stories.excerpt: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects has renewed its 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease at Gordon Property Group’s 860 Broadway. Selldorf has called the Flatiron District’s 860 Broadway home for the last two decades, according to landlord brokerage Colliers. The asking rent was not disclosed. However, the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $79.41 per square foot, with Class A office space asking an average of $97.22 per foot and Class B space asking $79.96 during the second quarter, according to Colliers data. Seth Hecht from Colliers represented Gordon Property in this deal, while the tenant was represented by Erik Schmall and Scott Weiss from Savills. “860 Broadway is one of Manhattan’s iconic office buildings, and its location continues to make it a highly desirable destination for creative and innovative companies,” Hecht said in a statement announcing the renewal. “When a firm as globally respected as Selldorf Architects commits to another decade in the building, it speaks to both the property’s enduring appeal and the long-term strength of this market.” Savills did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. “Our focus has always been on owning and operating buildings for the long term,” Tim Gordon, managing director of Gordon Property Group, said in the statement. “Creating an environment where great companies choose to stay and grow is the ultimate measure of our success, and we’re proud that 860 Broadway continues to earn that kind of commitment.” Selldorf Architects was founded by Annabelle Selldorf in New York City in 1988, according to the company website. The firm has worked on a number of prestigious projects, including the Frick Collection, the Chateau Haut-Brion — a 16th century estate near Bordeaux in France – and the Museum of Contemporary Art in San Diego. bullets: Selldorf Architects renews 13,815-SF lease at 860 Broadway (Flatiron) for 10 years; 20-year incumbent tenant.
Asking rent not disclosed; Midtown South Class A averages $97.22/SF (2Q data).
Office leasing; no relevance to multifamily development.
stories.summary: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects renewed its 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease at 860 Broadway in Manhattan's Flatiron District, where it has been located for the past two decades. The asking rent was not disclosed, though Class A office space in Midtown South was averaging $97.22 per square foot in the second quarter.
stories.impact: No relevance to multifamily development. Office lease renewal in Manhattan does not signal residential demand, capital flows, or zoning changes affecting apartment development.
